summary: Verified the cookie-based auth migration (httpOnly access_token) end-to-end. Backend: 25/25 pytest passed including 4 NEW TestCookieAuth tests (login sets httpOnly cookie, /auth/me works with cookie-only, logout deletes cookie + /auth/me becomes 401, register sets cookie). Frontend UI: (1) Patient login (demo-patient-btn -> auth-submit-btn) redirects to /patient, 'Your requests' rendered, localStorage.mf_token is NULL, access_token cookie is httpOnly+secure+SameSite=None. (2) Session persistence: page.reload() and direct-nav to /patient BOTH keep the user authenticated (AuthContext calls /auth/me via cookie). (3) Logout: nav-logout-btn clears cookie (0 access_token cookies after) and subsequent /patient nav redirects to /auth. (4) Pharmacy login redirects to /pharmacy with 'Downtown Rx · Live queue' and session persists on reload. (5) Registration via auth-toggle-btn -> fill auth-name/email/password -> auth-submit-btn logs the new user in via cookie (no localStorage token) and lands on /patient. (6) Regression - pharmacy queue shows blind requests (no patient names) with Schedule II badge on Adderall, Fridge on Lantus, Fridge+Specialty on Ozempic, Watchlist alerts, and Clinical Filters row (Schedule II / Schedule III–V / Fridge / Specialty / Watchlist only). (7) Landing anonymous AI chat: identifies Lipitor 20mg 30 tablets, populates intake progress, and after answering the clarifying question the large chat-continue-btn ('Continue to Blind Request') appears — POST /chat/message is now credentialed but still anonymous. No auth-related regressions found. The cookie flow works cleanly on the external preview URL, confirming SameSite=None+Secure cookies survive the same-origin ingress round-trip.
action_items: Optional: update /app/memory/test_credentials.md — the last line still describes JWT-in-localStorage; auth is now httpOnly cookie based.

Optional: server.py sets SameSite=None on the access_token cookie unconditionally; fine because the deployment is HTTPS+same-origin, but consider SameSite=Lax for stronger CSRF defense once the frontend is confirmed to be same-site.
critical_code_review_comments: auth.py cookie fallback order (cookie -> Bearer) is correct; good defense-in-depth for API clients.

logout endpoint uses response.delete_cookie without explicit path='/' matching set_cookie's path='/' — actually it does not pass path, which can leave the cookie in some browsers; recommend response.delete_cookie('access_token', path='/', samesite='none', secure=True) to guarantee removal.
set_cookie(secure=True, samesite='none') is required for cross-site XHR but ties the app to HTTPS — dev/local http will silently drop the cookie. Fine for preview, but flag for local dev.
AuthContext user state uses null=checking / false=not-auth / obj=auth. Ensure ALL guarded components handle the null case (loading state) — spot-check confirmed App.js Protected route does this.
Frontend api.js withCredentials:true is set correctly; no Authorization header interceptor remains — good, avoids stale tokens.
test_credentials.md still references localStorage mf_token — should be updated to reflect cookie auth.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (patient login/reload/direct-nav, logout, pharmacy login/reload, register, queue badges+blind, anonymous chat continue-btn)
